subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should native Podman be a permanently bundled core sandbox backend, or should it use the existing plugin sandbox-backend registry?
rationale: This is a new security-sensitive execution backend and determines the long-term ownership, release, configuration, and policy contract; source review alone cannot make that product-boundary choice.

options.title: Move Podman to a plugin
options.body: Keep the generic core registry and Docker behavior, with Podman packaging, runtime probing, doctor guidance, and documentation owned by an external or bundled plugin.

options.title: Approve a bundled core backend
options.body: Explicitly accept Podman as a core-owned sandbox engine and require exact-head upgrade, policy, and live-runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer native Podman support until the sandbox backend ownership model is resolved more broadly.

recommendation.title: Move Podman to a plugin
recommendation.body: Keep the generic core registry and Docker behavior, with Podman packaging, runtime probing, doctor guidance, and documentation owned by an external or bundled plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current shared container refactor and were requested to review this sandbox design.
